content_selection.rationale: The main picks hold up. The Anthropic ECDSA and quantum-circuit results are concrete and checkable, the Beam and DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 open-weight releases are real model news, and the CERT-In multi-provider incident, the White House task-force charter and the widely covered Meta crawling terms are good policy choices. Leaving out the Nadella essay (Oct 10) and repeated prior-brief items was correct. The main gap is that the brief has no chips or infrastructure coverage. My research shows two infrastructure stories inside the 48-hour window got broad coverage and were cut: Taiwan's $4B Texas supplier park and the Nscale Norway delay ahead of its IPO. The Nscale story also links directly to the Anthropic IPO thread the brief did run. Five of the 11 items center on Anthropic, which is heavy, though each one has some news value on its own.
content_selection.evidence: The brief has no hardware or infrastructure item, yet the candidate list shows 'Taiwan funds up to $4B Texas industrial park for Nvidia supply chain' and 'Nscale Norway data center six months behind schedule ahead of listing' both excluded and marked '(not fetched)'.

selection_disagreements.story: Taiwan funds up to $4B Texas industrial park for Nvidia supply chain
selection_disagreements.rationale: Bloomberg reported it on Oct 16, quoting Taiwan's economics minister Kung Ming-hsin, and Seeking Alpha, Yahoo Finance/24/7 Wall St, Interesting Engineering and FourWeekMBA all picked it up. It ties into Nvidia's stated supply limits: Jensen Huang has said Nvidia can fill only about 70% of demand. The brief had no chips or supply-chain coverage at all, so this deserved at least a headline-only slot.

selection_disagreements.story: Nscale Norway data center six months behind schedule ahead of IPO
selection_disagreements.rationale: Bloomberg's Oct 15–16 report was carried by Quartz, DCD and several other outlets. It says only 6.4 of 30 MW are running at Glomfjord ahead of an NYSE listing at up to a $35B valuation. Microsoft and Anthropic make up about 85% of Nscale's contract value, and Anthropic can cancel tranches if deliveries slip. That makes it directly relevant to the brief's Anthropic IPO and compute-commitment framing, and it was a stronger industry item than headline-only filler.

selection_disagreements.story: Sakana AI open-sources Agentic Scientist v3
selection_disagreements.rationale: David Ha announced it on Oct 15, inside the window. It is released under Apache 2.0 with an 88-page arXiv paper and an ALIFE 2026 oral acceptance, and AlphaSignal, AI Weekly and RuntimeWire covered it. It fits the brief's own autonomous-science theme (VERID, Claude quantum circuits) and should have been a headline-only item at minimum.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked almost every major claim in the brief against primary sources: Anthropic's two research posts, TechCrunch, the Reuters piece syndicated by Lufkin Daily News, the DeepSeek Hugging Face card, The Decoder, MarkTechPost, Google Research, and coverage of Reflection, CERT-In, the task force, Perplexity and Meta. Nearly all of them match exactly, including the specific numbers, dates, quotes and benchmark tables. The brief also correctly flags the DeepSeek free-window conflict (October 31 vs November 1), the SPACE attempt count (108 vs 118), and the Beijing open-weights report as unconfirmed. There are a few small problems. The brief calls the four top-bit-zero seeds 'prime-curve' seeds, but Anthropic just says 'four of the ten seeds', and the context suggests they were the binary-curve seeds, since Anthropic recovered the prime-curve states separately with LLL. Reuters says Q2 revenue 'more than doubled', which the brief softens to 'near-doubling'. I couldn't verify a few details: the 'export controls' remark from a White House official and CERT-In's 180-day log-retention recommendation.
factual_accuracy.evidence: Brief: 'four of the ten prime-curve seeds have a zero top bit in every 32-bit word' vs Anthropic: 'four of the ten seeds have a 0 in the top bit for all 20 words... The prime-curve seeds came from the same lrand48 generator but kept fewer bits of each output.'

length_format.rationale: The brief has 11 Headlines bullets, within the 8-15 range. It has 9 deep-dives (4 Research, 1 Products, 2 Industry, 2 Policy), within the 5-10 range, and it correctly omits the empty Benchmarks section. The per-item length target is not met, though: nearly every deep-dive runs about 8-11 sentences, well beyond the stated 3-6. That is a systematic over-shoot that makes the items less skimmable. The added 'Headline-only items' section is a minor structural addition outside the defined sections, but it is harmless.
length_format.evidence: The DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 deep-dive runs about 11 sentences, from 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is an updated post-training checkpoint...' through to 'Why it matters...'. The ECDSA item runs about 8 sentences.

dedup.rationale: Most of today's stories (ECDSA seeds, quantum circuits, Reflection Beam weights, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017, Replit, Perplexity SPACE, Meta crawling terms) do not appear in the 10-14, 10-15 or 10-16 editions. Four items connect to prior coverage, and each is explicitly labelled as a follow-up with a specific prior date. Each reports a genuinely new event: an investor valuation discussion, a CERT-In advisory, a task-force charter, and a different Google team's wet-lab framework. The Anthropic IPO item restates the $16.8B Q3 figure only as background for the new ~$1.5T valuation report, so none of these are bare rehashes.
dedup.evidence: "Some Anthropic investors discuss a roughly $1.5T IPO valuation, below the ~$2T previously expected — Follow-up: the Q3 revenue item in the 2026-10-15 brief"
